question.prompt: For all positive numbers \(x\) distinct from \(1,\) \[ \frac1{\log_3x}+\frac1{\log_4x}+\frac1{\log_5x} \] equals

solutions.explanation:
The different bases suggest changing all three terms to one base. Since \(x>0\) and \(x\ne1\), we can use \(x\) itself as that base. The change-of-base formula gives
\[
\frac1{\log_a x}=\log_x a
\qquad(a=3,4,5).
\]
Now the product rule combines the sum:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1{\log_3x}+\frac1{\log_4x}+\frac1{\log_5x}
&=\log_x3+\log_x4+\log_x5\\
&=\log_x(3\cdot4\cdot5)\\
&=\log_x60\\
&=\frac1{\log_{60}x}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The original denominators and \(\log_{60}x\) are nonzero because \(x\ne1\). Thus the answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Use a common logarithm base
